dimensions.assessment: Affects eligible entities including community-based primary care/behavioral health providers, crisis centers, public health agencies, U.S. territories, and Indian tribes, as well as individuals experiencing acute suicide risk.
dimensions.evidence: eligible entities to implement models for providing stabilization services to individuals with serious thoughts of suicide.

dimensions.assessment: Provides competitive grant funding and clinical stabilization services aimed at reducing or eliminating acute emotional crisis and imminent suicide risk.
dimensions.evidence: clinical intervention or treatment that-- (A) reduces or eliminates a state of acute emotional crisis; (B) reduces or eliminates clear and imminent suicide risk

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to fund the grant program.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act to create a new federal grant program, evaluation framework, and technical assistance mechanism.
dimensions.evidence: Title V of the Public Health Service Act is amended by inserting after section 520N (42 U.S.C. 290bb-45) the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes grants with a fixed term not exceeding 5 years that are non-renewable, spanning fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
dimensions.evidence: The term of a grant awarded under this section shall not exceed 5 years. Such term is not renewable.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a competitive 5-year grant program administered by the Assistant Secretary to support stabilization services for individuals with serious thoughts of suicide, authorizing $30 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
